# Read of unit U1a, goal an-alert-ends-with-its-situation (round 1)

Subject: the diff of U1a on goal/an-alert-ends-with-its-situation against base
8900ff270b055e4421a346b7afa5d5df36db1498, judged against the build brief
/Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/.inputs/b716378c59290d70ed7a8f0d60388b1d/build-brief.md
(FINAL revision 3). Threat model: trusted operators and agents; accidental defects,
regressions, crashes and contract drift.

Diff identity: /Users/wido/.metasystem/unit/20261107t002545-31ce2839b5/round-1/worktree.diff
has SHA-256 be6ac7efaf751355f0dd5b8cad01e873aa56ba230c2aed1152b1f3a7f6bd8f1b, as the
brief says. It is byte-identical to the launch read.diff. The prepared copy's working
tree matches it line for line (`git diff 8900ff270` plus the untracked test file).

## Verdict

AGREE. No material findings.

## Checklist item 1: every change the brief requires is present, correct and tested; nothing else changed

The diff touches `internal/steward/alert_episode.go`, `internal/steward/tick.go`, the new
`internal/steward/alert_situation_test.go` and `testing.json`. Each is accounted for below.

**D1 mechanism in `alert_episode.go` (diff lines 1-69).**
- `const breachStopAlertOwner = "breach-stop"` has a comment saying it names only retained
  records. No writer comes back.
- `openBreachStop(e)` is `Owner == breach-stop && !Cleared`, so the guard against undoing a
  person's clear (R-142-m1e) holds.
- `breachStopEnded(tree, id)` matches the brief's table:
  - nil tree → "";
  - `tree.Archived` with `State == StateDone` → `goal-done`;
  - any other archived state → `goal-abandoned`;
  - `tree.Live[id]` that is not `IsFencedClaim()` → `goal-not-stopped`;
  - a fenced claim, or an id not in the ledger → "".

  `TreeGoals.Archived` (`internal/goal/validate.go:42-50`) checks Done before Abandoned, and
  `IsFencedClaim` (`internal/goal/file.go:105-108`) is State claimed, with Claimed and
  StopFence both set. Both are as the brief anchors them.
- `resolveEndedBreachStops`:
  - takes `lockAlerts(…, lock.Exclusive)` and loads through `loadAlertEpisodesUnlocked`;
  - returns before `read()` when no open `breach-stop` episode exists;
  - returns the read error without writing anything;
  - for each episode with an open stop and a non-empty code, sets `Resolved/ResolvedAt`,
    `Cleared/ClearedAt` and `ClosedBy = code`, and saves through `saveAlertEpisode`.

  It never sets `ClearedBy` and never touches `Acknowledged`, and it deletes nothing. That
  is the brief's Contract.
- The health-episode paths in `updateAlertEpisodesWith` (`alert_episode.go:463-571`) skip
  every `Owner != ""` episode, so they cannot touch the resolved breach-stop records later.

**D1 wiring in `tick.go` (diff lines 250-318).**
- The field `ledgerStops func(string, time.Time) (goal.Projection, error)` is on
  `tickHealthDependencies`, with a nil-reads-nothing comment. The brief accepts the name
  `ledgerStops`.
- The call sits right after `updateSpendEpisodesWith` and before the lane-silent pass. It
  passes the pass clock (`healthNow()`) to both the ledger read and the resolution time.
- On any error it writes one stderr line ("old budget-stop alerts not ended: …") and the
  pass goes on. That is fail-closed, as the brief says.
- Both production compositions carry `ledgerStops: seatDependenciesForConfig(cfg).Project`:
  - `defaultTickContinuationDependencies`;
  - the extracted `tickHealthConfigDependencies(cfg)`. The old `completeTickHealthWithConfig`
    literal moved into it unchanged and gained this one line, and
    `completeTickHealthWithConfig` now calls it.
- `runTickAfterCustodial` (`tick.go:544-552`) overrides only `prober`, `probeRuntime` and
  `examineLedger` on `dependencies.health`, so the new field survives into the production
  pass.
- No production code sets `TickConfig.GoalProjection` (grep), so production reads through
  `defaultSeatDependencies().Project` (`seat_start.go:171-181`, which calls
  `goal.Project(endpoint, false, now)`). That is the same reader the health ledger already
  uses (`health_ledger.go:36`).
- `seatDependenciesForConfig` (`seat_start.go:611-627`) only builds closures. It neither
  recurses into `defaultTickContinuationDependencies` nor does any I/O when it is built.
- Five lines of the continuation literal were realigned by gofmt because the new key is
  longer. They are not semantic changes.
- The helm's partial pass (`tick.go:407-439`) still builds no `tickHealthDependencies`, so it
  does not run D1. This is the brief's OPEN 4.

**Tests 1 and 2 (`alert_situation_test.go`).**
- Both drive each production composition as built, through
  `completeTickHealthWithDependencies` (builder rule 17). They replace only the side-effect
  seams (rule 3).
- The only double is `cfg.GoalProjection`. In test 1 it fails the test on a second read, on
  a wrong root or on a wrong clock.
- Clocks are the bed's fixed `time.Date` base. Every test and subtest calls `t.Parallel()`.
  There is no sleep, no `time.Now` and no re-exec.
- Test 1 seeds D, X, A, F, U and a person-cleared D. It checks the three codes with
  `ResolvedAt == at`, that F and U stay open, and that the person's clear is kept. A whole
  `reflect.DeepEqual` against the seeds confirms that `Acknowledged*` and every other field
  are unchanged.
- Test 2 covers three cases:
  - zero reads with only health, pattern and person-cleared stop episodes;
  - a projection error: the episode is unchanged and the pass returns nil;
  - a nil tree.

**`testing.json`.** The only change appends the two new test names to
`supervision-bed-standard`, as rule 1 requires. That group's packages include
`internal/steward`.

**Runs on this read (host load 11-25):**
- `go test ./internal/steward -run 'TestBreachStopAlerts|TestTick|TestSpendFence|TestLaneSilent' -count=1`: ok.
- `go vet ./internal/steward`: ok.
- `go test ./internal/steward -count=1 -p 2` (the whole package, rule 13): ok, 349.8s.
- `go test ./cmd/metasystem -run '^TestAudit' -count=1`: ok, 36.1s. The new stderr line passes
  the message audit.
- The round's frozen check (`round-1/check-1818249964/output.log`) shows every landing group
  green, `unit/internal/steward` included, with `LANDING-CHECKED 0`. Its audits step exited 0.

**Mutations.** Each was applied through `go test -overlay`, so the worktree was not touched.
Each run was `-run TestBreachStopAlerts`.

| mutation | expected by the brief | observed |
|---|---|---|
| m1: drop the `IsFencedClaim` guard | both subtests of test 1 fail | both fail: "a stopped goal's alert ended while it was still stopped" |
| m2: drop the wiring in `defaultTickContinuationDependencies` | `continuation` fails | `continuation` fails: "old stops stayed open"; `config` passes |
| m3: drop the wiring in `tickHealthConfigDependencies` | `config` fails | `config` fails, and so do test 2's `ledger-error` and `nil-tree` cases ("ledger read 0 times") |
| m4: read the ledger before the open check | test 2 case a fails | `only-health-and-pattern` fails on the unexpected read |
| m5: return the read error from the pass | test 2 case b fails | `ledger-error` fails: "an unreadable ledger must not fail the health pass" |
| m6 (extra): ignore the read error and use the returned projection | not named | survives; see observation 1 |

Size: about 70 changed production lines (+48 in `alert_episode.go`, +22/-8 in `tick.go`,
5 of them gofmt realignment), against the estimate of 59. That is well under the 250 stop
line. The whole diff is about 250 lines against the estimated 320.

## Checklist item 2: the proof command's tests exercise the changed behavior, not only the happy path

The proof command is `/usr/bin/true`, so the proof itself exercises nothing. The frozen
check and the new tests carry the evidence. Beyond the happy path, the new tests cover:

- a fenced claim and an id not in the ledger, which stay open;
- a person's earlier clear, which is kept;
- the zero-read path;
- a ledger read error, which fails closed and leaves the pass green;
- a nil tree.

The mutation table shows that each guard the brief names is pinned.

## Non-gating observations

1. **Test 2 `ledger-error` does not pin "use nothing from a failed read" (m6 survives).**
   The double returns `goal.Projection{}` together with its error. The one seeded stop is
   also the unknown id, so an implementation that ignored the error and used the returned
   projection would still pass.
   - Why no customer impact: production `goal.Project` and `defaultSeatDependencies().Project`
     return `Projection{}` (a nil tree) on every error path, so the resolver would resolve
     nothing either way.
   - Possible fold, if wanted: return a tree in which the seeded goal is done, together with
     the error.
   - Severity low; not material.
   RELATION: new
2. **A pruned done goal's old alert stays open for good.** `goal prune` (`internal/goal/verbs.go:4339-4349`)
   deletes archived goals outside the retention closure. Such an id is then "not in the
   ledger", and the brief's table keeps it open. This is the brief's own decision, not a
   defect of the diff. It belongs on the later list next to OPEN 1-5 if the live count after
   both units lands short.
   RELATION: new
3. **A second ledger projection runs under the exclusive alerts lock on every full pass while
   any leftover stands.** On the lane, three fenced-claim leftovers keep one open until those
   goals resume. The brief accepts this cost ("Simplification: one lock …"). It is recorded
   so the cost is visible if `alert list` or `alert seen` latency shows up on the lane.
   RELATION: new
4. **The fail-closed stderr line repeats on every full pass while the ledger cannot be read
   and a leftover is open.** The brief specified this line. It goes to the tick's stderr,
   not to a person's channel.
   RELATION: new

## Budget

About 22 of the 48 reader tool calls were used. Every checklist item was checked in full.

VERDICT: land
